item.title: The McGill Daily: Keeping our unhoused community warm this winter

item.title: The McGill Daily – Anneke Goodwin: The Sexual Politics of the Trade War
item.dc:creator: Anneke Goodwin
item.description: As we have seen, there appears to be no video that can resurface, no picture that can be released, no assault Trump can commit on women that can seriously affect him in the polls. item.title: The McGill Daily – Lorin Kamaci: Princeton Professor Beth Lew-Williams Wins 2026 Cundill History Prize
item.dc:creator: Lorin Kamaci
item.description: During the forum, Lew-Williams explained that John Doe Chinaman began with questions about everyday life. After researching anti-Chinese violence and immigration restrictions in the 19th century American West, she realized how much was not known about the specifics of Chinese immigrant life in America. Could they enter a barbershop, for example? Where could they sit in a segregated theatre?

item.title: The McGill Daily – Stella Phipps: When “Boys Will Be Boys” Means Boys Killing Girls
item.dc:creator: Stella Phipps
item.description: In 2025, Netflix released psychological crime drama Adolescence, a British TV series that would change the way we think about the manosphere, online incel culture, and its implications on contemporary misogyny. The story, set in South Yorkshire, follows the arrest of a 13-year- old boy on suspicion of murdering his female classmate after she rejected his romantic advances.

item.description: Bryan isn’t an actual character in any of the games, but the fact that he is just an ordinary person makes him feel similar to most of the Resident Evil protagonists. item.dc:creator: Beau Milelli
item.description: Despite its growing presence on campus, the history of the website remains obscure; some peers I spoke to even thought it was an official McGill website. item.dc:creator: Amihan del Rosario-Tapan
item.description: From the dark of the stage, theatre artist esi callender speaks: “ Slave Play is a comedy of sorts. It should be playedas such. item.dc:creator: Maria Hamdaoui

item.title: Le Délit – Joséphine Miton : Un monde bâti sur du sable
item.dc:creator: Joséphine Miton
item.description: La demande mondiale de sable, qui a triplé entre 2000 et 2020, alimente un trafic illégal. Au Maroc, le PNUE parle même de véritables « mafias du sable ». Ces réseaux visent surtout les plages, dont le sable est facile à prélever et bon marché. Les vagues l’ont déjà lavé et calibré, et il ne reste qu’à le pelleter dans un camion. La plupart des plages marocaines appartiennent au domaine public.
